p01.why: Three declarations with equivalent heads and different parameter names; no main.

p02.why: Enumerations with fixed underlying types get their enumerators after the class body; GCC still rejects under Q-0199, which is settled.

p03.why: Every parameter type is structural, including double and an aggregate with public members.

p04.why: The member function template is defined with two heads; as<int> gives 2 and the pair holds 'a'.

p05.why: Defaults of each kind, and N's default names T.

p06.why: A constant pack typed by the type pack in the same head is not deducible; EDG rejects, Clang and GCC accept (Q-0195).

p07.why: Defaults from three declarations add up from right to left, so Triple<> is valid.

p08.why: An alias template has a default before a parameter with no default.

p09.why: The placeholder takes type void from (void)0, and void is not structural.

p10.why: Equal class arguments give one object, also across two templates, and unequal ones give different addresses.

p11.why: A constant parameter of type void.

p12.why: Template template parameters declared with class and with typename.

p13.why: A template template parameter pack with a default.

p14.why: One declaration has a pack and the other does not.

p15.why: One head with the parameters of both the class and the member template.

p16.why: The friend definition gives a default, and the call finds it by its argument, with T = int.

p17.why: The two heads have different numbers of parameters.

p18.why: Owner has a destructor that is not constexpr, so it is not a literal type.

p19.why: In an alias template the pack must be last.

p20.why: The constant parameter declaration defines an enumeration.

p21.why: auto takes the argument's type, and decltype(auto) keeps int& for (object).

p22.why: A member class is defined after the class body.

p23.why: A variable template has the name of a class template in the same scope.

p24.why: Back is deduced or defaulted after the pack, and in packs the trailing function parameter pack deduces Back; all three give 2.

p25.why: Unscoped member enumeration with a fixed type defined after the body; GCC still rejects under Q-0199, which is settled.

p26.why: A variable in the body has the name of the template parameter.

p27.why: Member operators defined after the class body; 3+5 is 8 and a<b.

p28.why: The parameter T hides the struct T inside the template only.

p29.why: Point has a constructor that is not constexpr and is not an aggregate.

p30.why: A member template in a local class.

p31.why: The default ends at the first >, so "4>" is left over.

p32.why: Pointer<T> is T*, so T deduces from &n.

p33.why: Pointers to void and to cv void are scalar types and so structural.

p34.why: A function template can have a default before a parameter without one; U is deduced.

p35.why: The > is in parentheses, and B is false.

p36.why: The pack in the argument list after the class name lacks ...

p37.why: Two declarations both give the default for T.

p38.why: Equal class arguments refer to one object across two templates, and unequal ones to different objects.

p39.why: The type that auto takes, Secret, has a private data member.

p40.why: Each specialization of the variable template is its own variable; a static member variable template works too.

p41.why: A call without arguments in angle brackets prefers the plain function; use<>(0) uses the template.

p42.why: A friend function template declaration that is not a definition gives a default.

p43.why: A destructor must not be a member template.

p44.why: Last is deduced from the call and the pack is empty.

p45.why: twice(3) prefers the plain function, and twice<int> has only the template as candidate.

p46.why: In a class template a constant pack typed by a type pack of the same head follows that pack.

p47.why: Each head uses its own inner default: int inside the class, char in the outside definition.

p48.why: Two declarators after a template head.

p50.why: One use of each kind of template; all checks hold.

p51.why: A class template definition followed by a declarator.

p52.why: Two uses of one alias specialization give one closure type on GCC and EDG, and two on Clang (Q-0200).

p54.why: Secret has a private data member.

p55.why: Defaults from two declarations add up: char and int.

p56.why: Back follows a pack, has no default, and no function parameter deduces it; EDG rejects, Clang and GCC accept (Q-0195).

p57.why: A member function template is virtual.

p58.why: In a variable template the pack must be last.

p59.why: The argument list after the class name swaps the order of the head's parameters.

p60.why: The constant parameters have different types.

p61.why: Unnamed parameters, and typename in a template template parameter.

p62.why: The other declarations have another function type or another head, so they are other templates; only the friend is viable.

p63.why: A constant pack with a default.

p64.why: class and typename mean the same thing, and parameter names can be left out.

p65.why: Templates and a plain function share a name; which(1.0) prefers the plain function.

p66.why: Assignment to a constant parameter of scalar type.

p67.why: A friend named after the parameter in a used class template; Clang and GCC accept, EDG rejects (Q-0198).

p68.why: Array and function parameter types become pointer types.

p69.why: U has no default in any declaration, yet T gets one; GCC accepts (Q-0296, settled).

p70.why: Another declaration of the friend function template with a default; EDG rejects, Clang and GCC accept (Q-0197).

p71.why: Template template parameters with a constant parameter and with a pack.

p72.why: Different arguments give different closure types.

p73.why: The outside definition leaves out the requires clause; EDG accepts (Q-0385, settled).

p74.why: The constant pack of the member template takes its type from the enclosing class's type pack.

p75.why: An int parameter is a prvalue, a reference is an lvalue, and a class is a const lvalue.

p76.why: A template with C language linkage.

p77.why: A member has the name of the parameter.

p78.why: const char S[] is const char*, and int F(int) is int (*)(int).

p80.why: The class template name takes its type from each argument by class template deduction.

p81.why: A namespace name B does not hide the parameter B, so sizeof(B) is sizeof(char).

p82.why: The alias specialization uses itself through a member of a class template.

p83.why: The member template does not override Base::use; through Base the virtual gives 1, and through Derived the template gives 2.

p84.why: A declaration of the same template before the friend definition with a default; EDG rejects, Clang and GCC accept (Q-0197).

p85.why: An explicit specialization with C language linkage.

p86.why: A typedef after a template head.

p88.why: The user guide gives Size<long> for 3, and the implicit guide gives Size<char> for 'a'.

p89.why: Each specialization has its own static member.

p90.why: In a class template the pack must be last.

p92.why: Top-level volatile and const are dropped from the parameter type.

p94.why: The template template parameters have heads that are not equivalent.

p95.why: Back follows the pack and has no default and no deduction; EDG rejects, Clang and GCC accept (Q-0195).

p96.why: A class template has a default before a parameter with none.

p97.why: Outside definitions with renamed parameters in order, and the pack with ...

p98.why: A partial specialization head can have parameters after a pack.

p99.why: The static member is defined after the body as 7, and the member initializer uses it.

p101.why: A class template has the name of its own parameter.

p102.why: A local class declares a friend template.

p103.why: The call chooses the plain twice(int), which has no definition, and the template never supplies one.

p104.why: The base B and the member Size hide the parameters of the same names; 16 and 8.

p105.why: Each explicit argument fits only one of the two templates.

p106.why: A non-static data member template in a class template.

p107.why: The address of a constant parameter of scalar type.

p108.why: Two parameters with one name in one head.

p109.why: A variable template has a default before a parameter with none.

p110.why: A type parameter and a constant parameter at one position.

p111.why: A class without a name after a template head.

p113.why: Tag deduces from Tag*, and named gets Tag explicitly; Id<Tag> gives no value.

p114.why: Point has a constexpr destructor, so it is structural; the object is never destroyed, and v is 1.

p115.why: const int N and int N declare the same parameter, and N is an int prvalue.

p116.why: Equal arguments give one object whose address is constant.

p117.why: A partial specialization with C language linkage.

p118.why: A storage class specifier on a constant parameter.

p119.why: Tag is in a non-deduced position of Id<Tag>, and no explicit argument or default gives it a value.

p120.why: A default in an outside member definition.

p121.why: Pointer<int> is int*, so the two declarations of take are one function.

p122.why: The outside definitions repeat the whole head; 4 + 3 = 7.

p123.why: A type pack with a default.

p124.why: The object has its value before dynamic initialization, so reader.seen is 7.

p125.why: Member templates of all four kinds in a class.

p126.why: A default in the member's own head in an outside definition.

p127.why: A variable has the name of a class template.

p128.why: A friend class template declaration with a default; Clang and EDG reject, GCC accepts (Q-0196).

p129.why: Each specialization has its own static member; a static member variable template is defined after the class.

p130.why: The outside definition's head gives C no inner default, so C<> is checked and rejected at the definition.

p131.why: A friend named after the parameter in a class template that is never used; every compiler accepts.
